The pin is tests/test_xml_specs.py:1296 test_the_flat_corpus_rule_is_documented, which asserts both docs/VERBS.md and the `auger spec --help` text contain "flat corpus" and "assertion-only".

items.criterion: PROOF: pytest tests/test_xml_specs.py::test_rejects_duplicate_dangling_stale_and_unregistered_test_refs -q prints 4 passed. FAILIF: a non-zero exit or fewer passed, meaning duplicate-id refusal weakened.
items.detail: Ran `python3 -m pytest "tests/test_xml_specs.py::test_rejects_duplicate_dangling_stale_and_unregistered_test_refs" -q` -> EXIT=0, output "4 passed in 0.04s" (the parametrized 4 cases at tests/test_xml_specs.py:636).

items.criterion: PROOF: grep -ci "assertion-only" docs/VERBS.md prints 1. FAILIF: 0 lines, meaning the author-facing rule paragraph is missing.
items.detail: Ran `grep -ci "assertion-only" docs/VERBS.md` -> "1". The line is docs/VERBS.md:666: "**The corpus is a FLAT CORPUS, and `<include>` is an assertion-only edge (AUG-147).** Membership is decided by the file system: every `*.xml` under ROOT contributes blocks and is selectable, whether or not any other document includes it..." (paragraph runs to :679).

items.criterion: PROOF: grep -c tests/test_xml_specs.py tests/gate.sh prints 2. FAILIF: any other count, meaning the new pins are not in the gate pytest arm.
items.detail: Ran `grep -c test_xml_specs.py tests/gate.sh` -> "2": line 157 (the AUG-118 comment) and line 206, the actual pytest arm `setsid timeout ... python3 -m pytest tests/test_auger.py ... tests/test_xml_specs.py ...`, so the new pins run under the gate's test_command (`bash tests/gate.sh`).

items.criterion: PROOF: git -C /home/kara/auger merge-base --is-ancestor 3150cea HEAD exits 0. FAILIF: a non-zero exit, meaning the documented fix is not on the graded tree.
items.detail: Ran `git merge-base --is-ancestor 3150cea HEAD; echo exit=$?` -> "exit=0". 3150cea is "fix(spec): document and pin the flat corpus; <include> is an assertion-only edge (AUG-147)" touching auger.py, docs/VERBS.md, tests/test_xml_specs.py (+150 lines).

items.criterion: The documented model matches the loader's actual behaviour: membership is filesystem discovery, include decides order, and include still asserts its target — not merely that a string exists in the docs.
items.detail: auger.py:7982-8030 `_spec_discover_documents` builds membership from `sorted(root.rglob("*.xml"))` with no include-edge filtering, so participation is discovery-only. tests/test_xml_specs.py:1227-1262 asserts the id SET is identical with and without the include while the ORDER differs (["INC-SH-1","INC-U-1","INC-ORPH-1"] vs ["INC-U-1","INC-ORPH-1","INC-SH-1"]), and :1263-1295 asserts the un-included orphan is selectable/assemblable while a dangling `<include src="does-not-exist.xml"/>` still exits 2 with `spec error (unresolved-include)`. Matches docs/VERBS.md:666-679.

items.criterion: The `auger spec --help` surface actually renders the flat-corpus paragraph (reachable from the CLI entrypoint), not only the docs file.
items.detail: Ran `python3 auger.py spec --help` -> prints "The corpus is a FLAT corpus: every *.xml under ROOT contributes blocks and is selectable, whether or not another document includes it. <include src> is an assertion-only edge — it splices that fragment's blocks at the include site (so it decides their ORDER) ...". Source: auger.py:13986-14000 (description= with argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter).

items.criterion: The new pins are not tautological: they exercise the real CLI against a temp corpus rather than asserting on doc text alone.
items.detail: tests/test_xml_specs.py:136-144 `run_spec` calls `auger.main(["spec", *argv])` in-process; the pins call run_spec("list"/"assemble"/"validate", ...) on a corpus built by flat_corpus()/write_corpus() in tmp_path (tests/test_xml_specs.py:1200-1295), so they assert loader behaviour, not prose.

items.criterion: The change does not regress the rest of the spec suite (full tests/test_xml_specs.py green).
items.detail: Ran `python3 -m pytest tests/test_xml_specs.py -q` -> EXIT=0, "58 passed in 1.11s".

items.criterion: The added docs/VERBS.md paragraph does not break the repo's docs arm (registry + tally checks).
items.detail: Ran `bash tests/docs_check.sh` -> EXIT=0, "PASS: README claims match code — fences ok ... VERBS.md registry ok, tally ok (14 tables), 5 env/path refs ok".
